name: Lal Ded (Lalleshwari)
credit: No portrait shown: no contemporary likeness of Lal Ded survives
bio: Lal Ded, also called Lalleshwari or Lalla, is the best-known woman poet of medieval Kashmir and a figure of the Kashmiri Shaiva tradition. She is traditionally placed in the fourteenth century, and the dates given here are the traditional ones; little is recorded of her life beyond the legends told about her. Her sayings, called vakhs, are short verses in Kashmiri on the self, the breath, devotion and the oneness of the soul with Shiva, and they are among the earliest writing in the Kashmiri language.

Her vakhs were handed down by memory and in manuscripts, and are still quoted in Kashmir by Hindus and Muslims alike. The English translations here are those made by George A. Grierson and Lionel D. Barnett in Lalla-Vakyani, or The Wise Sayings of Lal Ded (Royal Asiatic Society, 1920), which gives 109 vakhs; the numbering is the edition's own.
